name: Balinese Water Temples: the scale of coordination
description: Janssen's Fig. 1–2: the subaks in 1, 2, 7, 14, 28 or 172 groups each share one plan and start month, found by hill-climbing (exhaustively for 1 and 2 groups; otherwise from the better of random plans and the best single plan for everyone), then fixed for ten years; the harvest over years 6–10, under each reading of the subak–dam columns. Level 2 is our two rivers (Janssen's highlands and lowlands are not in the data); level 28 has 22 groups in the data. Measured (release, seeds 1–3, all alike, recorded 2026-09-29), levels 1 → 172: Janssen's code's columns: low rain 26.41, 26.41, 26.41, 26.50, 26.44, 26.81; middle 27.05, 27.05, 27.05, 27.09, 27.09, 27.25; high 27.33, 27.33, 27.33, 27.36, 27.34, 27.43. Physical columns: low 23.06, 23.06, 23.58, 24.04, 24.06, 24.68; middle 25.79, 25.79, 25.79, 25.99, 26.00, 26.75; high 26.64, 26.64, 26.64, 26.74, 26.75, 27.22 t/ha/yr. Finer coordination always helps, but by 0.3–1.5 % under the code's reading, where water rarely binds; under the physical reading water binds at low rain and the rise reaches 7 %. Janssen's rise from ≈ 17.5 to 22.8 (+30 %) appears under neither, and the temple scale (14) is never best. Slow: each 172-group search takes about ten seconds.
